 Business Paytm’s Discipline Era: How Vijay Shekhar Sharma Traded Blitzscaling for Profit and Won Back the Street
 In Short
 Explore how Vijay Shekhar Sharma transformed Paytm’s strategy from blitzscaling to disciplined growth, cost efficiency and profitability, rebuilding investor confidence.
 Karthik Prasad Created On:   3 Nov 2026 7:11 PM IST Brand Buzz Comment Share :
 X Paytm’s Discipline Era: How Vijay Shekhar Sharma Traded Blitzscaling for Profit and Won Back the Street
 A− Font size A+ Select Hans India Now FOLLOW ON G o o g l e News Across India's fintech landscape, the era of growth-at-any-cost is giving way to a harder test: can scale be turned into profit? Paytm and its founder Vijay Shekhar Sharma, once emblematic of the startup boom's "scale first, profits later" mantra, are now offering an answer that is increasingly reflected in both the company's earnings and Wall Street's assessment of its future. 
 Paytm's latest quarterly numbers show a company increasingly focused on operating leverage, cost discipline and profitable growth. Revenue rose 28% year-on-year to ₹2,648 crore in Q2 FY27, while EBITDA climbed 90% to a record ₹270 crore, up 33% sequentially. EBITDA margin expanded to 10.2%, crossing double digits for the first time. Financial services revenue grew 49%, while payments revenue rose 25%. Profit after tax stood at ₹225 crore. 
 Sharma captured the shift during the latest earnings call, declaring that Paytm had moved beyond the question of whether it could become profitable. The focus, he indicated, is now on building a business where revenue growth and operating efficiency reinforce each other. 
 The key is the widening gap between revenue and costs. While Paytm continues investing in growth, its overheads are expanding much more slowly. JM Financial noted that indirect expenses grew 13% year-on-year against revenue growth of 28%, bringing indirect costs down to 46% of revenue from 52% a year earlier. The brokerage described the trend as “AI-led leverage outruns reinvestment” and raised its FY27-FY28 EBITDA estimates by 2-9%. 
 The discipline is also visible in how Paytm approaches growth. Rather than pursuing transaction volumes at any cost, the company is prioritising profitable merchant relationships, better pricing and higher-margin payment products. Nomura noted that Paytm's Q2 performance reflected deliberate decisions to prioritise payment economics, while maintaining its Buy rating and raising its target price to ₹2,300 from ₹2,250. 
 AI sits underneath that math. Paytm is deploying AI across customer acquisition, servicing, collections and internal operations, improving productivity while supporting growth. Despite continued investments in sales, marketing and technology, EBITDA margin has risen from 6% in FY26 to 8.3% in Q1 FY27 and 10.2% in Q2 FY27. 
 Morgan Stanley sees this combination of growth and execution creating further value. Following Q2 FY27, the brokerage upgraded Paytm from Equal-weight to Overweight and raised its target price by 35%, from ₹1,450 to ₹1,950. It also increased its FY28 and FY29 EBITDA estimates by 30% and 22%, respectively, citing stronger financial services momentum and improving earnings visibility. Axis Capital also raised its target price to ₹1,950 from ₹1,490 while maintaining its Buy rating, reinforcing the growing confidence among brokerages. 
 The debate around Paytm has shifted accordingly. For years, the question was when the company would turn consistently profitable. With two consecutive quarters of expanding EBITDA margins in FY27, the conversation is increasingly about how far its profitability can compound as the business scales. 
 Paytm's approach to growth reinforces that change. Its expanding merchant network, financial services distribution business and improving payment margins are creating opportunities to generate more revenue from existing relationships, while AI helps contain the cost of expansion. For a company built during India's blitzscaling years, the emerging story is no longer simply about scale. It is about how much profit that scale can generate.
